hints.title: Choose which variable is fixed
hints.body: For each fixed x, you are allowed to find a suitable y. Rearrange the expression as x+(1−x)y.
hints.recap: The existential choice of y can depend on x.
hints.pitfall: You are not asked to find one y that works for all x.
hints.pause: Consider this expression as a straight line in y.

recall.reminder: Read the order of fixed inputs and permitted choices.

hints.title: Investigate the line’s range
hints.body: With <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> held fixed, inspect the slope <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>. Consider positive, negative and zero slope separately. For each case, determine which outputs the expression can reach as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow></math> ranges over all real numbers.
hints.recap: A line’s slope determines how its output changes as its input varies.
hints.pitfall: Check a zero coefficient before dividing by it.
hints.pause: Determine the ranges and identify which parameter cases still need direct substitution.

recall.reminder: A line’s slope determines how its output changes as its input varies.

hints.title: Complete the existence test
hints.body: For each nonzero-slope case, try solving for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow></math> after setting the expression equal to a chosen negative target. Separately evaluate the original expression at any parameter value that made the slope zero.
hints.recap: Algebraic division and direct substitution address different coefficient cases.
hints.pitfall: A formula involving a denominator cannot settle a parameter value that makes that denominator zero.
hints.pause: Verify your proposed choices, settle the zero-slope case, and determine how many inputs satisfy the statement.

recall.reminder: Algebraic division and direct substitution address different coefficient cases.

solution:
For x≠1, choose y=−1−x1−x. Then x−xy+y=x+(1−x)y=−1<0.

For x=1, the expression is always 1, so no y works. Exactly one real x is excluded. Answer E.
knowledgePattern: Existence of a negative value of a linear function of y
